study type: repeated cross-sectional analysis, interrupted time series analysis
cohort: The study included 2,122,267 nulliparous individuals from publicly available U.S. birth certificate data with singleton pregnancies, cephalic presentation, no chronic hypertension, diabetes, or fetal anomaly, who delivered between 39 and 42 weeks' gestation.
finding: An increase in induction of labor at 39 weeks' gestation in individuals with BMI ≥40 was not associated with a decrease in the cesarean delivery rate.
mod_finding: For individuals with BMI <40, the post-ARRIVE period was associated with a decreased rate of cesarean delivery, whereas for those with BMI ≥40, no significant decrease in cesarean delivery rates was observed.
cross-section timing: From 2015 to 2021, with pre-ARRIVE period from August 2016 to July 2018 and post-ARRIVE period from January 2019 to December 2020.
